# ADR-0009 build plan — ingestion (generated by adr-plan, 2026-07-30)

**Re-cut 2026-07-30 for the ADR-0009 amendment** (v1 collapses the platform
tier into the long-tail tier): 11 slices, 6 phases. Two slices deferred
behind the platform-volume revisit trigger: `declarative-scraper-engine`,
`llm-selector-repair`. The LLM extractor is promoted from the last phase to
the source edge; the R2 vault moves up with it (extraction reads vaulted
HTML). Critical path:
`observation-contract → raw-persist-dedup → per-source-normalizers →
entity-resolution-merge → lifecycle-events → ingest-health-gates`

Provenance: adr-plan workflow run `wf_c0aebe68-1d0` (3 phases: Decompose →
13 parallel Assess agents → Plan synthesis); per-slice assessments recovered
from the run journal. Re-cut applied by hand from the amendment — the
original 7-phase cut is in git history (`ff7d11e`).

## Phases

1. **observation contract + pipeline skeleton** — `observation-contract`
   (solo; the sole dependency root — get stage interfaces right for
   replayability + per-source pluggability; design care here beats verify
   cycles).
2. **raw layer + source edges** — `raw-persist-dedup` (first real Drizzle
   migration; canonical-JSON hash stability is the trap), `r2-html-vault`
   (promoted: HTML is vaulted + hashed *before* extraction),
   `rescuegroups-adapter` (off critical path; key pending).
3. **extract + normalize + validate** — `llm-extractor` (promoted from
   phase 7: the sole scraping edge, behind a provider interface),
   `golden-fixture-eval-harness` ⚠ verify (built together with the
   extractor — it is the model-selection mechanism), `per-source-normalizers`.
4. **entity-resolution-merge** — the lone hard-reasoning slice ⚠ verify:
   per-field tier-then-recency merge, provenance JSONB, idempotent under
   replay. Silent Tier-1 clobbering passes naive tests — adversarial pass
   required. Kernel exists (src/core/trust.ts); v1 may be single-source-
   dominant with the fuzzy matcher as a designed seam.
5. **lifecycle-events** ⚠ verify: per-source disappearance scoping; a
   failed run must never mass-emit `animal.disappeared` (bogus rows are
   permanent in the sacred event_log and would falsely trigger the
   adoption-evolution moment). Must land before health gates so
   stale-marking uses event rows, never UPDATEs.
6. **health gates + retrieval** — `ingest-health-gates` (né
   scraper-health-gates; now also wires the fixture-eval canary into the
   daily cron tick), `retrieval-jobs` (parallel).

## Per-phase detail: code choices and why

### Phase 1 — observation contract + pipeline skeleton
`observation-contract` · opus, medium effort, no verify

- **What gets built.** `Observation` type
  (`{ source, externalId, payload, fetchedAt, contentHash }`) in
  `src/core/`, plus the shared four-stage pipeline every source feeds:
  persist-raw → normalize (LLM extraction is a normalizer — see phase 3) →
  entity-resolve → update-canonical + emit events, as composable stage
  interfaces with stub implementations. Adapters implement only the
  fetch edge that emits observations.
- **Code choices.** Stages are plain typed functions/interfaces, not a
  framework. Two properties are load-bearing: stages must be **replayable**
  (extraction/normalization can re-run over the retained corpus without
  re-fetching — this is what makes LLM nondeterminism recoverable) and
  **per-source pluggable** (a new source is one adapter + one mapper, zero
  pipeline edits).
- **Why opus / no verify.** A bad abstraction fails loudly downstream, but
  it's the graph's single point of failure — budget goes to design care up
  front, not verify cycles after.

### Phase 2 — raw layer + source edges (parallel opus batch)

**`raw-persist-dedup`** · medium, no verify — *on the critical path*

- **What gets built.** Migration adding `content_hash` + `last_seen` to
  `raw_payloads` — the first real Drizzle migration (roadmap item 1
  carry-in). Insert logic: new raw row only when the hash changed,
  otherwise a cheap `last_seen` touch.
- **Code choices.** Canonical-JSON serialization for the hash (stable key
  order, no volatile fields) — **hash instability is the trap**: a false
  dedup match silently drops corpus signal; a never-matching hash bloats
  the corpus. The `last_seen` UPDATE is the one sanctioned mutation on an
  append-only table — document it in the schema comment. RescueGroups rows
  keep the ADR-0006 purge tag; consented-scrape rows stay fully sacred.
- **Why no verify.** Mechanical; hash stability is directly unit-testable.

**`r2-html-vault`** · low, mechanical — *promoted from phase 3*

- **What gets built.** Scraped HTML archived to an R2 vault bucket, object
  key stored on the raw row (keys-not-blobs, same pattern as ADR-0003
  photos); lifecycle/retention note added to `doc/infra.md`.
- **Why promoted.** Under the amendment, extraction *reads* vaulted HTML —
  vault-then-extract is what makes the LLM extractor replayable, so the
  vault must exist before the extractor. Needs an S3-compatible client
  (none yet — `@aws-sdk/client-s3` or `aws4fetch`; **dependency ADR**).
  Remember the runbook's `NO_CHECK_BUCKET` note for bucket-scoped tokens.

**`rescuegroups-adapter`** · medium, no verify — *off the critical path*

- **What gets built.** RescueGroups fetcher (v5 preferred, v2 fallback)
  paging the API and emitting observations; register the `ingest.poll`
  pg-boss job in the slot commented in `src/worker/index.ts`.
- **Why off-path.** Normalizers test against golden fixtures, so this can
  slip while the key application is pending. Failures are loud; raw
  payloads are verbatim + replayable, so mapping bugs are recoverable.

### Phase 3 — extract + normalize + validate

**`llm-extractor`** · medium, no verify — *promoted from phase 7*

- **What gets built.** The sole scraping edge: fetch page → vault HTML to
  R2 → send (lightly stripped) HTML to an LLM behind a provider interface
  (`extract(html, schema) → json`, same pattern as the ADR-0004 image
  pipeline) → schema-validate → emit observation. Per-page cost and
  validation-failure metrics ship with it (ADR-0010 Postgres-as-metrics) —
  the "cost/error stops being noise" revisit trigger must be observable,
  since it's now also the platform-tier re-activation trigger.
- **Code choices.** Schema validation via zod (**dependency ADR**).
  Provider choice is empirical: the fixture harness scores DeepSeek-class /
  batched Haiku / one larger ceiling model; cheapest passing model wins.
  Batch API is a fit for the daily poll (latency-insensitive, 50% off).
  Optional token-trimming (strip nav/script boilerplate before sending) —
  a light HTML parser if fixtures show it pays; not required to ship.
- **Why no verify.** LLM output can be schema-valid yet wrong, but the ADR
  deliberately bounds that with the harness + health gates rather than a
  perfect first pass — the bounds are the sibling slices.

**`golden-fixture-eval-harness`** ⚠ verify · medium — *built with the extractor*

- **What gets built.** Fixture format: saved HTML (and saved API payloads)
  + hand-checked expected canonical output — **one per onboarded site,
  verified by a human** (Logan + Claude at onboarding). A vitest-runnable
  harness diffs extractor output against truth. The project's third eval
  harness and the first to ship; now also the **model-selection mechanism**
  and a dry run for the item-8 text-faithfulness harness.
- **Two roles, kept distinct** (per the amendment): run on prompt/model/
  provider changes (regression gate) and as a cheap canary on the daily
  cron tick (frozen snapshots — proves the mechanism, not today's pages;
  live pages are phase 6's job).
- **Why verify.** An overly permissive comparator (missing-field
  tolerance, loose equality, partial-fixture pass) silently green-lights
  hallucinated extraction — the costly-subtle-bug profile exactly. Extra
  weight now that the harness also picks the production model.

**`per-source-normalizers`** · medium, no verify — *on the critical path*

- **What gets built.** Per-source mapper interface (raw payload →
  canonical fields), starting with the RescueGroups mapper, plus a
  **replay command**: iterate the retained corpus in `fetchedAt` order,
  idempotent, rebuilds only the derived canonical layer, never touches
  `raw_payloads` or `event_log`. The LLM extractor's output re-enters here
  like any source's; replay covers both.
- Conflict logic is deliberately NOT here — fenced into phase 4.

### Phase 4 — entity-resolution-merge (the lone Fable slice) ⚠ verify
high effort, hard-reasoning, adversarial verify pass required

- **What gets built.** Merge of normalized observations across sources
  into `animals`, resolving conflicts **per-field** by trust tier then
  recency, writing `{ source, fetchedAt }` provenance JSONB per field,
  idempotent under corpus replay.
- **Code choices.** Reuse the tested kernel `src/core/trust.ts`
  (`resolveFact`/`resolveFacts`, deterministic ties). v1 may be
  single-source-dominant — the fuzzy cross-source matcher is a **designed
  seam** (interface + trivial same-source impl); real fuzzy dedup is
  roadmap item 10.
- **Why Fable + adversarial verify.** A merge that lets a fresher low-tier
  observation silently clobber a Tier-1 fact **passes a naive test suite**
  and corrupts canonical truth invisibly.
- **Scheduling.** The chokepoint — phases 5–6 are blocked behind it.
  Start the moment normalizers land.

### Phase 5 — lifecycle-events ⚠ verify · opus, medium

- **What gets built.** Per-run set-diff against canonical state, appending
  `animal.seen` / `animal.updated` / `animal.disappeared` to `event_log`;
  adoption inferred from disappearance.
- **Why verify.** Three edges a plausible naive diff ships wrong:
  disappearance must be **scoped per source**; a partial/failed run or
  tripped health gate must **never mass-emit** `animal.disappeared`;
  reappearance ordering matters. Bogus rows are permanent in the sacred
  event_log and would falsely trigger the adoption-evolution moment.
- **Ordering.** Before health gates, so stale-marking has event vocabulary
  instead of UPDATEs.

### Phase 6 — health gates + retrieval (parallel opus batch)

**`ingest-health-gates`** · medium, no verify — *scope widened*

- **What gets built.** Per-run gates on the LLM extractor (and any future
  edge): schema-validation failure rate, items-found vs. expected,
  required-field coverage, plus sanity invariants on fresh output (counts
  don't crater, species don't flip, names non-empty). Trip → source
  disabled + flagged, nothing ingested, listings marked stale via event
  rows. Also wires the **fixture-eval canary** into the daily cron tick.
  Fail loud into the event log (ADR-0010 boring alerts).
- **Why no verify.** Trip conditions are explicit thresholds —
  unit tests on them suffice.

**`retrieval-jobs`** · medium, no verify

- **What gets built.** pg-boss jobs triggered by event_log inserts building
  chunks + embeddings referencing subject ids; the pgvector `vector`
  column + FTS tsvector migration deferred from scaffold lands here.
- **Code choices.** Enqueue-on-write over LISTEN/NOTIFY (simpler,
  sufficient at this volume). Embeddings are derived and rebuildable
  (ADR-0003), so migration-safety weight doesn't apply.

### Deferred (platform-volume revisit trigger)

- **`declarative-scraper-engine`** — config-driven selector extraction for
  uniform platform widgets. Activates when one platform exceeds ~50–100
  pages/day or LLM cost/error stops being noise.
- **`llm-selector-repair`** — the AI-as-mechanic repair loop; only
  meaningful once the declarative engine exists.

## Effort calibration (from assessments)

- Fable + adversarial verify: **entity-resolution-merge only**.
- Verify but not Fable: lifecycle-events, golden-fixture-eval-harness.
- Everything else explicitly does NOT warrant verify — failures are loud
  or structurally gated; don't over-spend.

## New dependencies this plan implies (each needs an ADR)

- S3-compatible R2 client (`@aws-sdk/client-s3` / `aws4fetch`) — phase 2.
- zod for LLM-output schema validation — phase 3; likely worth adopting
  for the observation contract too if adopted at all.
- LLM extraction provider key(s) (DeepSeek and/or Anthropic) — phase 3;
  behind the provider interface, chosen by the fixture harness.
- (Optional) light HTML parser for pre-extraction token trimming —
  phase 3, only if fixtures show it pays.

## Sequencing risks

1. observation-contract is the single point of failure — bad stage
   abstraction taxes all downstream slices.
2. Nail content-hash stability before adapters run at volume (false dedup
   silently drops corpus signal).
3. Vault-before-extract is an ordering invariant, not a preference — an
   extractor that reads live HTML without vaulting first breaks
   replayability and makes LLM misses unrecoverable.
4. Phase 4 is the chokepoint — start it the moment normalizers land; the
   RescueGroups adapter is OFF the critical path and can slip.
5. lifecycle-events before health gates (append-only bright line).
6. The fixture harness must land with (not after) the extractor — it's
   how the production model gets picked; shipping the extractor on an
   unmeasured model inverts the amendment's "empirical, not aesthetic"
   rule.
